title: Binary patching of one-degree coefficient improvements relative to a supplied global witness
statement:
Let $D$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $D\to A$ a map of commutative rings, and $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ a separated finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions]. Let $Y=U\cup V$ be a cover by two quasi-compact open subschemes [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Fix $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{Y_A})$ [def-pc-derived-category] and $n\in\mathbf Z$, where $Y_A=Y\times_D\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For $W=U,V,Y$ and a commutative $D$-algebra $E$ with a specified map $E\to A$ over $D$, write $W_E=W\times_D\operatorname{Spec}E$, $q_{W,E}:W_E\to\operatorname{Spec}E$, $\pi_{W,E}:W_A\to W_E$, $K_W=K|_{W_A}$, and $M_E=\widetilde A[0]$ on $\operatorname{Spec}E$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. For every integer $m$, define $\mathcal A_m(W)$ to mean that there exist such an $E$, finite type over $D$, an object $G\in D(\mathcal O_{W_E})$ with bounded coherent cohomology [pqf-def-coherent], and a morphism $\delta:G\to R\pi_{W,E*}K_W$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image], for which the following normalized morphism has cone with quasi-coherent cohomology and zero $H^i$ for every $i\ge m$ [def-weil-triangulated-category]:
$$\theta_{W,E,G,\delta}:Lq_{W,E}^*M_E\otimes^{\mathbf L}G\longrightarrow R\pi_{W,E*}K_W.$$
Here derived pullback and tensor are [def-pc-derived-pullback, def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]; $\theta_{W,E,G,\delta}$ is the adjoint [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-adjoint] of
$$L\pi_{W,E}^*(Lq_{W,E}^*M_E\otimes^{\mathbf L}G)\simeq L(q_{W,E}\pi_{W,E})^*M_E\otimes^{\mathbf L}L\pi_{W,E}^*G\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{W_A}\otimes^{\mathbf L}K_W\simeq K_W,$$
where the middle arrow uses the given $A$-structure on $W_A$ and the adjoint of $\delta$. Suppose a specific global object $F\in D(\mathcal O_Y)$ with bounded coherent cohomology and a morphism $\gamma:F\to R\pi_{Y,D*}K$ are given, and that the cone of $\theta_{Y,D,F,\gamma}$ has quasi-coherent cohomology and $H^i=0$ for every $i\ge n+1$. Here $Y_D=Y$ and $D\to A$ is the original coefficient map. If $\mathcal A_n(U)$ and $\mathcal A_n(V)$ hold, then $\mathcal A_n(Y)$ holds. The local witnesses may use different finite type $D$-algebras. The assertion concerns one degree of improvement of this supplied global witness; it assumes no compatibility between the chosen local witnesses and prescribes no restriction of the output witness. Ring maps need not be flat, and $K$ need not be relatively pseudo-coherent.

Ann. 198, pp.287--316, primary descente proof WANTED.

proof.text: If $Y=\varnothing$, take $E=D$, $G=0$, and $\gamma=0$. Every module sheaf and every cone on this scheme is zero. Otherwise $Y$ is Noetherian, quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and it is separated as a scheme because it is separated over an affine scheme. Its bounded-coherent object $F$ is pseudo-coherent. Perfect approximation at cutoff $n$ gives a perfect $Q\to F$ whose cone is zero in all degrees $i\ge n$.

proof.text: Use the dg coefficient model $\mathcal B$ and let $T(P)=\Phi_D(P)=\mathcal B\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}^{\mathbf L}P$. The comparison lemma identifies the supplied normalized arrow with $\nu_D(\gamma)$ on underlying complexes. Compose with $T(Q)\to T(F)$ and call the resulting dg-linear arrow $t:T(Q)\to\widehat K$. Its cone $C$ is quasi-coherent. Tensor with $A$ over the constant sheaf $D$ preserves an upper cohomological bound, so the cone of $T(Q)\to T(F)$ is zero for $i\ge n$. The triangle of cones of the composite therefore gives $H^i(C)=0$ for $i>n$, using the supplied bound for the original witness. This replacement does not assert flatness of $Y/D$.

proof.text: Choose finitely many affine opens $T_j=\operatorname{Spec}S_j$ covering $Y$, each contained in either $U$ or $V$. Their rings are finite type over $D$; choose $Q_j=D[x_1,\ldots,x_{r_j}]\twoheadrightarrow S_j$. Restrict a witness for $\mathcal A_n(U)$ or $\mathcal A_n(V)$ to $T_j$. Open restriction, affine direct image and the normalized comparison give a finite type $D$-algebra $E_j$, a bounded-coherent module complex $L_j$ over $S_j\otimes_D E_j$, and a map whose scalar-action cone is zero for $i\ge n$. Thus we retain genuine restriction of the given local arrow; no common coefficient stage or overlap transition is chosen.

proof.text: Set $Q_{j,E}=E_j[x_1,\ldots,x_{r_j}]$ and $Q_{j,A}=A[x_1,\ldots,x_{r_j}]$. The ring $Q_{j,E}$ is Noetherian and surjects onto $S_j\otimes_D E_j$. Hence $L_j$ has bounded finite cohomology over $Q_{j,E}$ and admits a bounded-above finite-free representative over that ring. Its scalar tensor is $Q_{j,A}\otimes_{Q_{j,E}}^{\mathbf L}L_j=A\otimes_{E_j}^{\mathbf L}L_j$: a bounded-above free $Q_{j,E}$-resolution is also $E_j$-K-flat, since $Q_{j,E}$ is free over $E_j$. It becomes a bounded-above finite-free $Q_{j,A}$-complex. The scalar-action map to $K_j$ is a morphism in $D(Q_{j,A})$; forgetting to $Q_j$ gives precisely the normalized local arrow by the affine pullback/tensor formula. Since its cone is zero for $i\ge n$, truncating the finite-free source sufficiently far below $n$ proves that $K_j$, restricted to $Q_{j,A}$, is $n$-pseudo-coherent.

proof.text: The affine restriction of $Q$ has bounded finite cohomology over the Noetherian $S_j$ and hence over its Noetherian polynomial source $Q_j$. The same finite-free resolution argument shows that $T(Q)|_{T_j}$, with its $Q_{j,A}$-action, is pseudo-coherent. Use the comparison node's polynomial restriction: $Q_j\otimes_D R_A\to Q_{j,A}$ is a quasi-isomorphism since $Q_j/D$ is free, so its derived equivalence takes this dg-linear arrow and its cone to $D(Q_{j,A})$. The cone criterion, with source parameter $n+1$ and target parameter $n$, makes $C_j$ $n$-pseudo-coherent. Step 2 gives $H^i(C_j)=0$ for $i>n$, so top-cohomology finiteness gives a finite $Q_{j,A}$-module $H^n(C_j)$. The dg action on $C$ makes this an $S_j\otimes_D A$-module: it factors through $H^0(\mathcal B|_{T_j})=S_j\otimes_D A$. A generating list over $Q_{j,A}$ is then also a generating list over this quotient.

proof.text: Take a termwise quasi-coherent complex representing the underlying $C$ on $Y$ and smart-truncate it above $n$; its last term is the quasi-coherent sheaf of degree-$n$ cycles. On each affine $T_j$, lift the finite generators of $H^n(C_j)$ from step 5 to sections of these cycles; surjectivity on sections follows from the exact affine module equivalence. The $S_j$-submodule generated by those finitely many cycles defines a finite-type quasi-coherent subsheaf on $T_j$. Extend it as a finite-type quasi-coherent submodule of the global cycle sheaf, separately for each $j$, and take the finite sum $N$. Since $Y$ is Noetherian, $N$ is coherent. Inclusion of cycles gives $a_0:N[-n]\to UC$. The image of $H^n(a_0)$ generates $H^n(C)$ after multiplication by $A$, as is checked on every $T_j$.

proof.text: The coherent object $N[-n]$ is pseudo-coherent on the Noetherian scheme $Y$. Perfect approximation at cutoff $n$ supplies $P\to N[-n]$ with $P$ perfect, $H^i(P)=0$ for $i>n$, and $H^n(P)\twoheadrightarrow N$. Compose with $a_0$ to get $a:P\to UC$. Extension--restriction adjunction for $\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal B$ gives $\widetilde a:T(P)\to C$. The coefficient comparison includes this adjunction. Since $R_A$ is nonpositive and $D$-K-flat, $T(P)$ is zero in degrees $>n$, and its top cohomology is $A\otimes_D H^n(P)$: in a nonpositive resolution the top total degree is the cokernel of the two adjacent differentials, hence the ordinary tensor of the two top cohomologies. The map on that cokernel sends $b\otimes x$ to $bH^n(a)(x)$. Step 6 therefore makes $H^n(\widetilde a)$ surjective. Thus $J=\operatorname{Cone}(\widetilde a)$ is zero for $i\ge n$.

proof.text: Form the homotopy pullback $H=\widehat K\times_C^h T(P)$ in the dg category, using $\widehat K\to C$ from step 2 and $\widetilde a$. Concretely $H=\operatorname{Cone}(\widehat K\oplus T(P)\to C)[-1]$, where the map is the difference of those two arrows. The mapping-cone triangles are $T(Q)\to H\to T(P)\to T(Q)[1]$ and $H\xrightarrow{u}\widehat K\to J\to H[1]$. Both $T(Q)$ and $T(P)$ are perfect over $\mathcal B$: their local finite perfect models are scalar extensions of the ordinary ones. Closure under cones makes $H$ perfect. The second triangle and step 7 show that $H^i(Uu)$ is an isomorphism for $i>n$ and is surjective for $i=n$. In particular $H^i(Uu)$ is surjective for every $i\ge n$. This records the cohomological-epimorphism hypothesis needed in the next step.

proof.text: Apply finite coherent factorization of a cohomological epimorphism to $H,u$ and $m=n$, using the surjectivity established in step 8. It supplies a finite type coefficient algebra $D\to E\to A$, bounded-coherent $G$ on $Y_E$, an ordinary scheme-derived arrow $\delta:G\to R\pi_{E*}K$, and $\sigma:H\to\Phi_E(G)$ such that $\nu_E(\delta)\sigma=u$ and $H^i(U\sigma)$ is surjective for all $i\ge n$. Write $v=U\nu_E(\delta)$. For $i>n$, the composite $H^i(v)H^i(U\sigma)=H^i(Uu)$ is an isomorphism and the first factor out of $H^i(UH)$ is surjective; hence $H^i(U\sigma)$ is also injective and $H^i(v)$ is an isomorphism. In degree $n$, surjectivity of the composite gives surjectivity of $H^n(v)$. The long exact cone sequence now gives $H^i(\operatorname{Cone}(v))=0$ for every $i\ge n$. Quasi-coherence is part of the comparison. No approximation of $H$ by an arrow pointing into $H$ is used.

proof.text: The comparison identifies the underlying $\nu_E(\delta)$ with $Rp_{E*}\theta_{Y,E,G,\delta}$, for exactly the scalar-action adjoint specified in the statement. The projection $p_E:Y_E\to Y$ is affine. Its derived direct image on quasi-coherent complexes detects the cohomological bounds, so step 9 implies that the cone of $\theta_{Y,E,G,\delta}$ is quasi-coherent and zero for every $i\ge n$ on $Y_E$ itself. Together with the finite type algebra $E$, bounded-coherent $G$ and ordinary arrow $\delta$, this is $\mathcal A_n(Y)$. All comparisons are derived. The argument does not impose a restriction of $G$ on $U$ or $V$, and only used the existence of their two supplied local witnesses.
